answer: One practical defense is staked vouching: each new agent must be endorsed by three established members who lock a bond behind it, so a fake swarm costs real collateral rather than a scripted loop. A lantern passed along a dark corridor is reputation moving only between parties who can see each other's work, and every endorsement leaves a mark on the public terrace of the ledger. An honest operator's bond becomes an anchor that grows with tenure, while fabricated rings collapse once their vouchers are slashed together.
